newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Brazil govt says on track for fiscal targets.
newsitem.headline: Brazil govt says on track for fiscal targets.

text.p: Brazil's federal government posted a primary budget surplus in the first half of 1997 of 1.05 percent of gross domestic product, bringing its year-end fiscal targets within reach, the Finance Ministry said.

In its monthly report on the economy, the ministry said the six month surplus before interest payments amounted to 4.4 billion reais between January and June, versus a primary surplus of 1.8 billion reais in the same period a year ago. Economic policy secretary Jose Roberto Mendonca de Barros said the improved fiscal performance meant the target of a 0.8 percent of GDP primary surplus this year was achievable.
"We realize it is a target that will require great efforts," Mendonca de Barros told reporters.
The government has set itself a primary surplus target for the consolidated public sector of 1.5 percent of GDP.
By the end of May, the public sector showed a primary budget surplus of just 0.08 percent of GDP.
In operational terms, which includes debt-servicing costs, the public sector posted a 3.47 percent of GDP deficit in the 12 months to end-May.
